text.p: Stone Energy Corp said Wednesday Amoco Corp has drilled and placed on production a jointly-owned development well located offshore Louisiana in Eugene Island Block 224.

During a six hour test, the C-1 Well flowed at the average daily rates of 1,100 barrels of oil and 2.9 million cubic feet of natural gas with a flowing tubing pressure of 6,200 pounds per square inch, Stone Energy said.
The company also said its evaluation of the Smith Goodrich Cocke No. 1 Well, located onshore in Iberia Parish, La., allowed an increase of 150 barrels daily in production there.

Stone Energy operates and owns an interest in Eugene Island Block 243, immediately south of Amoco's Block 224. The C-1 Well, located about 650 feet from the lease line, was drilled to a total depth of 14,752 feet and logged about 150 feet of net pay in six sands.

The joint development and sharing arrangement, which includes portions of both blocks, was structured in part to minimize the total investments in potentially competitive reservoirs. Working interests in the joint area are owned by Amoco, 50 percent; Stone Energy, 43 percent, and partnerships managed by Stone Energy, seven percent.

Stone Energy said future joint plans include a second well scheduled for the third quarter of 1997 that is designed to develop reserves from this newly-proved fault block and to test an additional objective which produces in adjacent fault blocks.

It said the Smith Goodrich Cocke No. 1 Well was drilled to 10,300 feet and tested for a limited duration at the average daily rates of 1,954 barrels of oil and 1.0 million cubic feet of natural gas with flowing tubing pressure of 1,227 pounds per square inch on a 11/64 inch choke. The well encountered a total of about 366 net feet of oil productive sand.

The company said the evaluation of the productive section resulted in an extension of the proved limit of the reservoir from which the Cocke Goodrich No. 3 Well is producing. Based on this interpretation, the company has increased the daily producing rates from the Cocke Goodrich No. 3 Well to 800 barrels of oil and 500,000 cubic feet of natural gas from 650 barrels and 400,000 cubic feet.
First production from the SGC No. 1 Well is expected in late June after unitization, or earlier if an escrow agreement can be reached with the drillsite lessor, Stone Energy said.

The company owns a 100 percent working interest and a 76 percent net revenue interest in the SGC No. 1 Well before well payout, and, depending on unitization results, expects to have a 90 percent working interest and a 69 percent net revenue interest after payout. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
